title: Mission: your own photos, measured
drDigitalIntro:
Photos have a shape and a size, and knowing that is the difference between 'this picture will not fit' and knowing why.
• You will pick two photos from your own computer: one wider than it is tall, and one taller than it is wide.
• The page reads each one's real width and height and shows them to you. It measures them here on your machine and never sends them anywhere.
• Then you will rename a photo to something meaningful and pick that one, and the page will turn it down if the name is still the one the camera gave it.
• IMG_4471 means nothing in five years. 'Dad at the lake' still means something.

playgroundTask.goal: You measured and named your own photos

steps.say: Find a photo on your computer that is wider than it is tall.
steps.detail: A landscape, a group of people, most things taken with the camera held sideways. The page will tell you exactly how many dots across and down it is.

steps.say: Now find one that is taller than it is wide.
steps.detail: A portrait of one person, a tall building, almost anything taken with a phone held upright.

steps.say: Make an album and put three or four related photos in it.
steps.detail: A trip, a person, an occasion. An album does not move or copy the pictures — it is a second way of looking at the ones you already have.

steps.say: Rename one photo to something that says what it is, then pick that one.
steps.detail: Rename it in your photo library or your file manager first. Then press the button and choose it. A name starting with IMG or DSC will be turned down, because that is the camera talking, not you.

drDigitalSuccess: Two shapes, an album, and one photo that will still make sense to you in ten years.
drDigitalHint: The shape is decided by the picture itself, not by how you are looking at it. If a photo is turned down, the page tells you its real width and height so you can see why.
